messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] TRUNCATED message when running part2
messages.body_plain:
Hi Stuart,
Functions g.part2 and g.part4 do not write csv files anymore. Functions g.report.part2 and g.report.part4 inside the package have taken over the reporting generation functionality. The users of function g.shell.GGIR would not have noticed the difference as for them there is no change in interface or functionality.

Note that function g.part2 and g.part4 only produce .RData-files which are stored in the 'meta'-folder. The RData files contain all the data needed to build the reports.

To generate the reports you would need to either have to: (option 1) load the RData files, extract information you are interested in and generate your own report or (option 2) use g.shell.GGIR with argument do.report=c(2,4). In the latter case it should be possible to re-use previously generated RData-files from g.part2 and g.part4 for this. To do that you would first have to pilot run g.shell.GGIR on a few files to create the required folder structure after which you can move all the RData-files to the newly generated folder structure.

Sorry I should have reported this in the package update overview. I made these changes to split the computational part (g.part2) from the summarising and plotting part (g.report.part2) in order to make it easier to process accelerometer files in parallel.
Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Stuart,
If you do not explicitly specify do.anglez=TRUE as input argument the
code assumes that you are not interested in the z-angle, because the
default is do.anglez=FALSE.
However, if you  tell the code to run parts (modes) 1, 2 and 3 via the
g.shell.GGIR function then the code is clever enough to automatically
decide to extract the anglez because it will know that you are
interested in sleep.

So, the only way to address this is by re-running part 1 and
explicitly stating that you need do.anglez=TRUE.

In the example file you sent me there is no z-angle included and in
the re-analyses there should be a z-angle in the variable names as
shown with the command: names(M$metashort).

Note that if you specify do.anglez=TRUE as a new input argument then
the line needs to end with a comma before the #comment starts:
28: do.anglez=TRUE , #for sleep anysis
29: chunksize = .... ,
Best wishes,
Vincent

Wear time is collected in the milestone data produced by part2 (RData format).

Variable IMP$rout[,5] gives you for every 15 minutes a 0 or a 1 to indicate whether the time segment was considered valid(0) or invalid (1). Next this should be all you need to describe hour by hour the activity patterns and non-wear time.
Best,
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Several questions + error with Part 4 Reporting
messages.body_plain:
Hi Taren,

1. Can you inspect the pdfs that are generated and stored in subfolder meta/sleep.qc/... Do these make sense to you? For example, do you count the expected number of nights, and is the sustained inactivity indicator (bottom colored line) up when you would expect it? Secondly, can you check whether the error occurs for all your datasets and files or just for one specific file or dataset? If yes, try to verify what makes that dataset different.

2. If you always expect a specific number of days of measurement then you could try variable 'strategy =  3' with ndayswindow specified. I developed this for a study where they sent the accelerometer by mail to the participant without knowing exactly when the participant would start wearing the monitor. If that doesn't work for your study design then split your dataset in subsets such that each subset has more or less the same number of non-wear hours at the beginning of the measurement. Inspecting the pdf plots produced by part 2 may help you here. Next, process each subset with strategy =2 and hrs.del.start set specific to that subset.

3. See response by Stuart... also note that all the epoch by epoch values are stored in the RData milestone data. So, if you or someone around you is a bit familiar with R you can extract this information yourself. IMP$metashort as produced by part2 has all the epoch by epoch acceleration values.

4. To some extend the code facilitates sensitivity analyses to a variety of parameters, but I did not facilitate this for all parameters assuming that for most of them people do not even want to run sensitivity analyses. To do this there are currently two options: (1) Run the analyses multiple times with different parameter settings and make a copy of the intermediate outputs. (2) Make a copy of the entire output folder after you have run part1 and then run part 2, 3 and/or 4 for each copy of the output separately. To do this make sure that the various copies of the output folder have a name that starts with 'output_' followed by an informative description xx about what you intended to do with them. Next, set argument studyname to xx and make sure that xx matches the xx in "output_xx". Also, set argument datadir to c(). In that way the code will consider each copy of the output folder as a separate study, named xx.

Vincent
